rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's thirty builder trees go (a row of queen palms, torrey pines and corals every 6 m along the back fences, two fan palms 3 m from the house fronts, magnolias, jacarandas and others by the yards); seven come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: by the picnic table, the chairs, the grills and the beach umbrellas, and on the open lot corner.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 13 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the big open lot corner, 35 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the west back yard with the adirondack chair and the beach umbrella: a coral tree over them
the back yard with the adirondack chair and the gas grill: a magnolia over both
the east back yard by the closed beach umbrella, 43 m on: the same
the north yard with the adirondack chair and the gas grill: a coral tree over them
